- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, overestimate the price spike; correct by adding 2–5% to forecast if recent events are bullish and supply net is negative.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and forecast is rising, overcorrect by subtracting 3–8% from forecast if supply net is positive or events are neutral.
- After a sharp spike in price (true outcome > 85), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment persists, model tends to underestimate true price; add 5–10% to forecast if recent events are bullish and sentiment > 0.7.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average if true outcome deviates > 5% from forecast.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is bearish and supply net is negative, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 2–5% if true outcome is below 75% of forecast.
- If recent events are bullish and supply net is positive, model often underestimates price; add 3–7% to forecast if sentiment > 0.7 and supply net > 0.
- When sentiment is bearish and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 3–7% if sentiment < 0.3 and supply net < 0.
- If forecast is rising steadily and true outcome is flat or falling, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–4% per day if sentiment is mixed or bearish.
- For 30d forecasts, if sentiment is bullish and supply net is negative, model often underestimates; add 5–10% to forecast if sentiment > 0.7 and supply net < 0.
